# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v2)
Date: 2026-11-16
(Supersedes everything in old/, which is disregarded per Morgan.)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Operator constraints
From Morgan's notes and inbox, taken as given:
- Solo, evenings and weekends only.
- Up to $2,000 of personal savings this year — not more.
- Skills: decent writing, okay Python.
- Day job (Dorrance Logistics) has a contract clause requiring disclosure/approval of outside roles and public statements made in a professional capacity. Annual disclosure due 30 Nov 2026. Until that's resolved, Morgan's name should not go out in public posts, press, or signed letters. This constraint is treated as hard, not optional, until Morgan says otherwise.

## What's neglected vs. not, for an operator with these constraints
- **Newsletter:** saturated — The Safety Ledger and others already aggregate well. A new one adds little on the margin.
- **Small-grants program:** $2,000 is too small to matter alongside rounds already running at $5k–25k (Emberfall) or compute-credit programs (Compute Commons). Not a fit for this budget.
- **Reading group:** low leverage, not differentiated, better as a side activity than the core bet.
- **Independent evals of a currently-unmeasured property:** fits the stated skills, produces one concrete reusable artifact instead of diffuse activity, can be scoped and started privately (no public exposure needed until write-up time), and has real outlets once finished (Alignment Commons call for posts, Compute Commons credits to run it, possibly Emberfall funding to resource it).

**Conclusion: make evals the initial bet.** Everything else (grants, letters, press, a newsletter) is opportunistic and secondary, not the main line of work.

## Near-term plan
1. Morgan completes the Dorrance outside-activities disclosure (due 30 Nov) — his call, his contract, not something this agent should do for him.
2. In parallel, scope one specific eval target with help from Priya Raman's landscape scan (requested 2026-11-16).
3. Once the disclosure is resolved, revisit the held-for-now public items: Pagewell site publish, Corvid open letter, press quote, Emberfall application, FMIR docket comment — all currently blocked only on the "name goes public" question, not on quality or readiness.
4. Build the actual eval once scoped; publish write-up under an open license; submit to Alignment Commons.

## Open items
See PENDING_APPROVAL.md — nothing there has been executed without Morgan's sign-off, except the domain renewal (explained there).

# Draft public comment — Docket FMIR-2026-0042 (NOT SUBMITTED)
Closes 20 Nov 2026. Comments on frontier-rule-comments.org are published together with the filer's name — confirm whether anonymous/unaffiliated filing is permitted if you want to comment without attribution.

---

I support the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule, with three suggestions:

1. Reporting should cover near-miss safety incidents during training and deployment, not only realized harms — near-misses are where the most useful information usually is.
2. The rule should specify a standard severity taxonomy so reports are comparable across labs and over time, rather than each filer inventing their own categories.
3. A public, structured summary registry (even if underlying incident detail is restricted) would let independent researchers notice patterns the labs themselves aren't positioned to see.

---
PLACEHOLDER NOTE: these are generic starting points, not yet your real position — edit before submitting. Also note this will be published with your name; consider timing relative to the Dorrance disclosure.
